description: Thin margins, brutal labor math, and a media narrative that flatters chefs and ignores everyone else. Ask about volume, consistency, and the economics, and skip anything resembling a question about passion for food.

questions.text: Anyone can execute one perfect plate. What does it take to do four hundred without a miss?
questions.lands_because: Names consistency under volume as the real skill, which is the industry's own definition of excellence and the opposite of the television version.
followups: Where does it break down first when it breaks down?

questions.text: Take me through the ten minutes when a service starts going wrong.
questions.lands_because: Time-bounded, high-adrenaline, and vivid on audio. Everyone in the industry has lived it and can narrate it beat by beat.
followups: Who pulls it back - and is it always the same person?

questions.text: A full dining room does not mean a profitable one. Where does the money actually go?
questions.lands_because: Leading with the correction proves you understand the economics, and operators are eager to explain food cost, labor, and rent to someone who will listen.
followups: What is the decision you make purely for margin that you wish you did not?

questions.text: What is the relationship between front of house and back of house really like?
questions.lands_because: The central social divide of a restaurant, including the pay asymmetry between tipped and non-tipped staff. Asking about both halves signals you know there are two.
followups: Does the tipping structure make that worse?

questions.text: What has changed about staffing since 2020, and what did the industry learn or refuse to learn?
questions.lands_because: Labor is the live issue in the industry, and the 'refuse to learn' clause invites a real assessment instead of a defensive one.
followups: What are you doing differently as an employer?

questions.text: What is the guest behavior that never makes it into the review but shapes the whole night?
questions.lands_because: Flips the review-driven power dynamic and lets the guest speak from the other side of it, which is both cathartic and genuinely informative.
followups: What does a genuinely good guest do?
